starts without this one's messages.

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-count-horizontal-runs
description: Use for ARC grids with separated horizontal runs of colors 3 and 2. Count runs, then encode their colors in a 2x3 output.
---

# Count horizontal color runs into a 2x3 grid

Use when an ARC input is mostly a uniform background and contains isolated horizontal bars of colors 3 and 2, with a small 2x3 output expected.

## Rule

1. Count each maximal contiguous horizontal run of color 3 as one object, regardless of its length or location.
2. Count each maximal contiguous horizontal run of color 2 as one object, regardless of its length or location.
3. Create a 2x3 output. Fill row-major with all the counted 3s first, then all the counted 2s. Leave remaining cells as 0.

The demos showed the input background can vary; it does not affect the count. Do not count individual colored cells or use bar lengths. The rule was verified on examples with counts (3:4, 2:1) -> `[[3,3,3],[3,2,0]]`, (3:2, 2:2) -> `[[3,3,2],[2,0,0]]`, and (3:3, 2:3) -> `[[3,3,3],[2,2,2]]`. If counts could exceed six, seek another demo or inspect the task-specific convention before assuming truncation.",
